title: National pollinator survey reveals insects’ favoured flowers
summary: Eight years of UK flower counts put ivy first for average insect visits among the 14 target flowers. The findings also underline different trends among pollinator groups.
why: Connect flower choice, survey design and seasonal resources when planning habitat management or field projects.

title: How IPM is helping Vietnam’s tomato farmers manage invasive tomato leafminer
summary: A greenhouse demonstration in Vietnam brings monitoring, sanitation, natural enemies and selective interventions together to tackle tomato leafminer, alongside practical training for growers.
why: A useful applied case study for evaluating biological control, farmer learning and the limits of demonstration trials.

title: Pest management in Ecuador: knowledge and access to alternatives
summary: CABI examines how farmer knowledge and access to pest-management alternatives can help reduce pesticide risks in Ecuador.
why: Explore the social and practical barriers that shape whether IPM is adopted beyond the trial plot.

title: An entomologist working with software engineers to improve farming
source: Entomology Today · Entomological Society of America
summary: An early-career profile follows Clay Morrow from plant–insect interactions and statistics into open-source whole-farm modelling, with pest-management features planned for future development.
why: See how entomology, quantitative skills and collaboration can combine in a research career.

title: Three new pollinator records in the Scottish Borders
summary: Surveys on council-managed sites found new vice-county records of Rose Chafer, Blue Mason Bee and Hairy-footed Flower Bee in the Scottish Borders.
why: Discuss why a new record can reflect improved detection or range expansion, and how records inform management.

title: A new home for entomological methods and ethics
summary: The first papers in Approaches in Entomology introduce a fully open-access journal covering methods, research philosophies and ethics across insect science.
why: A useful reading destination for research design, reproducibility, insect welfare and dissertation methods.

title: A conservation boost for two rare Devon ants
summary: A three-year partnership will improve heathland habitat, establish additional colonies and monitor Narrow-headed and Erratic Ants at Devon nature reserves.
why: Consider how habitat restoration, translocation and monitoring fit together in species recovery plans.

title: Honey bee veterinary medicine: a growing specialty
source: Entomology Today · Entomological Society of America
summary: A US-focused overview explores the growing role of veterinary expertise in managed honey bee health, alongside barriers in training, access and cost.
why: Connect bee pathogens, husbandry and professional practice, while distinguishing US policy from UK arrangements.

title: Phenotypic divergence is driven by mobile genetic elements in a heritable insect symbiont
summary: A mobile plasmid in the aphid symbiont Regiella was required for protection against a fungal pathogen, linking microbial evolution to differences among aphid populations.
why: Connects insect–microbe interactions, evolutionary biology and variation in susceptibility to fungal natural enemies.

title: Ninety-year trends reveal sharpest insect declines in the mid-twentieth century
summary: Swiss records spanning nine decades suggest that major butterfly and deadwood beetle declines preceded many modern monitoring programmes, with later trajectories differing between groups.
why: A useful case study for interpreting biological records, shifting baselines and conservation targets.

title: Pollinator functional group responses to urban land cover in Merseyside, UK
summary: An exploratory modelling study found that predicted habitat suitability for bee and hoverfly functional groups varied across urban land cover, including some densely developed areas.
why: Offers a UK example for discussing functional traits, species distribution models and the limits of habitat predictions.

title: The audience shapes the information content of the honey bee waggle dance
summary: Honey bees communicated food direction and distance less precisely when suitable dance followers were scarce, showing that the audience influences the signal.
why: An accessible update to animal communication teaching and a good example of testing a familiar biological explanation.

title: Limited thermal tolerance in tropical insects and its genomic signature
summary: Measurements across approximately 2,300 tropical insect species revealed restricted scope for lowland communities to increase heat tolerance, alongside strong differences among insect lineages.
why: Links physiological limits, evolutionary relationships and climate-change vulnerability in a broad comparative study.

title: Biocontrol potential of Metarhizium spp. against Myzus persicae and beet mild yellowing virus in the post-neonicotinoid era
summary: Controlled experiments found that Metarhizium isolates killed aphids and that fungal colonisation of sugar beet was associated with reduced beet mild yellowing virus loads.
why: Provides a case study in fungal biocontrol while inviting discussion of strain effects and the evidence needed before field application.

title: Mosquito–capsid interactions contribute to flavivirus vector specificity
summary: The study identified molecular interactions within mosquitoes that help explain why particular mosquito species differ in their compatibility with flaviviruses.
why: Connects insect physiology to vector competence and shows why vector–pathogen relationships require species-specific evidence.
